cases.finding: Scores enforcement and propagation of pre-existing governance decisions. It does not exercise legitimate ultimate-policy or identity authority making a new decision and returning it to operation.

Exercises role/value conflict reasoning, but the evaluated model is not established as the legitimate ultimate authority of an organization and no adopted policy decision is required to govern subsequent operation.

Provides executable value-conflict tasks and measures values expressed by tool-using agents. It does not establish legitimate organizational authority to settle identity/ultimate policy and bind later operation.

Agents legislate operational smart-contract rules inside a constitutional economy, but foundational contracts and key constitutional parameters are human-authored/agent-immutable. The evaluated legislation is below the ultimate foundational authority layer.

Provides governance/conformance scoring and stress evidence, including constitutional and authority questions, but does not itself execute an identity-level conflict through legitimate amendment/adjudication and then observe later operation under the changed policy.

Defines an end-to-end governance process that can adopt policy and amend the constitution under supermajority rules. It is useful S5 protocol evidence but not a benchmark of an agent harness's S5 capability.

cases.artifact: Agent Parliament constitutional ratification and amendment history
cases.finding: The public constitutional record documents an actual v0.1.6 ratification and later v0.1.7 amendment entering force through a declared legitimate authority process with supermajority voting, Crown veto/signature handling, version and hash provenance, separation-of-duty requirements and preserved amendment history. This is unusually strong S5-shaped evidence that ultimate organizational policy can actually change under an authority process, but it is a live governance record rather than a reusable agent-harness benchmark and supplies no matched canonical-harness capability comparison.

Defines a non-bypassable human escalation/decision path that can support Parent-governed S5 when the escalated issue is identity/ultimate-policy level, but the protocol itself is not a benchmark result.

First-party tests exercise proposer/ratifier separation, tiered legitimate authority, formal ratification, constitution-version change, authority-registry mutation and root-authority guards. This is strong S5-shaped mechanism evidence at the library boundary, but it is a conformance/regression suite rather than a reusable matched cross-harness benchmark, and the repository is not currently a canonical Index system.

Learns structured rule sets through specialized accept/edit/reject agents and task reward. Constitution optimization is measurable policy adaptation, but the evaluated system is not established as the legitimate ultimate-policy authority of an organization resolving an identity-level tension, so reward improvement does not establish direct S5 closure.

Benchmarks cooperation, autonomy, integrity and fairness under constitutional governance regimes, but the constitution is supplied as a fixed filtering/optimization layer. The experiment measures operation under policy rather than legitimate authority deciding or amending ultimate policy.

Benchmarks evidence-grounded public-policy simulation and downstream impact prediction. Its object is external policy analysis, not the evaluated harness's own organizational identity or ultimate-policy authority, so it is outside direct S5 capability measurement.
